Battle of Cannae
Part of the Second Punic War
Date2 August 216 BC
LocationCannae, Apulia; open ground beside the Aufidus river
ResultDecisive Carthaginian victory[1]
Belligerents
Roman RepublicCarthage
Commanders and leaders
Lucius Aemilius Paullus (KIA)

Maharbal
Strength
86,000 engaged[2] about 50,000 engaged, of whom 10,000 cavalry

between 48,000 and 70,000 killed
10,000 captured		 5,700 killed

The Battle of Cannae was fought on 2 August 216 BC.[3]

Prelude

Rome had raised 87,000 men in the theatre, but not all of whom reached Cannae.
